candidates: When defining TypeScript interfaces for diagram data objects (e.g. in `packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/common/commonTypes.ts`), audit actual call sites to determine which fields are genuinely optional before adding `?`. Do not mark all fields optional just to suppress TypeScript errors — only fields that are truly nullable or omittable at every call site should carry `?`; fields that are always required must remain non-optional to preserve type-safety guarantees.

When a JS-to-TS migration reveals a runtime bug — for example, a comparison against the string `'undefined'` (e.g. `x !== 'undefined'`) that should instead be a check against the value `undefined` (i.e. `x !== undefined`) — explicitly call it out in the PR description as a bug fix rather than treating it as an incidental refactoring detail. This helps reviewers understand the behavioral scope of the change and decide whether additional testing or a separate fix PR is warranted.

When a JS-to-TS conversion includes any change that could alter runtime behavior (even a small bug fix), run the project's end-to-end tests (`pnpm run e2e`) against the branch, comparing outputs against a `develop` baseline, before merging — to confirm that no diagram rendering outputs change unexpectedly.
